title: The error budget
prompt:
Implement `error_budget(slo_success_rate, total, failures, window_days=30)`:

- allowed failures = `total * (1 - slo)`; budget remaining = `1 - failures/allowed`, floored at 0 (1.0 when allowed is 0 and there are no failures)
- returns `{'slo', 'actual' (measured success rate), 'budget_remaining', 'status'}`
- status: `'healthy'` when remaining >= 0.5, `'burning'` when 0 < remaining < 0.5, `'breached'` at 0 (a real breach must NOT read as merely burning)

This function is the SLO decision: healthy → ship features; burning → stabilize.

tests.name: healthy, burning, breached
tests.code:
r = error_budget(0.99, 1000, 3)
assert r['status'] == 'healthy' and abs(r['budget_remaining'] - 0.7) < 1e-9
r = error_budget(0.99, 1000, 6)
assert r['status'] == 'burning' and r['budget_remaining'] > 0
r = error_budget(0.99, 1000, 20)
assert r['status'] == 'breached' and r['budget_remaining'] == 0.0
print('ok')
tests.hint: 20 failures exceeds the 10-failure budget: breached, not burning.
